people.narrative: Leslie Kean is the journalist who twice moved the entire subject, and both times the mechanism was the same: she got named officials to say on the record what had previously only been said privately. On 5 June 2023 she and Blumenthal published David Grusch's claim that the United States operates a multi-decade UAP crash retrieval and reverse-engineering programme holding craft of non-human origin, a story the New York Times did not run and which The Debrief published instead. That editorial fact is itself data about the structure of the coverup: the paper of record that had carried the 2017 story would not carry the 2023 one. Kean's 2010 book UFOs: Generals, Pilots and Government Officials Go on the Record, with a foreword by John Podesta, established the on-the-record method she has used since. She spoke at the inaugural Sol Foundation conference at Stanford in November 2023, placing her inside the academic-institutional wing of the movement as well as the journalistic one.
people.tierRationale: Tier A: author of the two stories that define the modern record, and a documented bridge between journalism and the Sol Foundation's institutional effort.

people.narrative: George Knapp is the longest-running investigative thread in this entire story and the one whose sourcing runs directly into the alleged program rather than around it. A Peabody and Edward R. Murrow winner at KLAS-TV in Las Vegas, he broke Bob Lazar in 1989 and put Area 51 into global consciousness. That single act of journalistic matchmaking is arguably the most consequential thing any reporter has done in this field. He attended the July 2023 congressional hearing, co-hosts the Weaponized podcast with Jeremy Corbell, and hosted the Netflix docuseries Investigation Alien in November 2024. Rolling Stone called him the 'John the Baptist of the UFO movement', which is dismissive but structurally accurate: the modern effort has his fingerprints at its origin.
